inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: Of the 10 children's records evaluated, five lacked the address of the emergency contact,
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: Of the 10 children's records evaluated, one lacked authorization for emergency medical care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Physician Information (26 TAC §746.605(11))

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: A child's food allergy plan has not been signed by a health care professional.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: Based on information obtained during the DFPS investigation, the director is not ensuring the operation is always operating in compliance with Minimum Standard rules.  There was evidence to support that unenrolled children are allowed to be at the daycare and participate in activities provided by the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The door handle to the bathroom in one classroom does not allow the door to be easily opened when inside of the bathroom.  The bathroom door in a second classroom is hard to open for children and staff from the inside and outside.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance: Based on information obtained through interviews, this standard was found to be deficient. Children are being placed in a bathroom as a discipline method.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance (26 TAC §746.2803(4))

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Appropriate to Child's Level of Understanding: Based on the information obtained through interviews, this standard was found to be deficient. Caregivers are using a reflection mirror as a discipline method for 3-5 year old children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Discipline - Appropriate to Child's Level of Understanding (26 TAC §746.2803(2))

occurrences.finding: Posting of Activity Plan: In one of the pre-k 4 rooms and one of the pre-k 3 rooms, the activity plans were not posted. This was corrected when the plans were posted on the wall.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting of Activity Plan (26 TAC §746.2209)

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Cleaning supplies were observed to be in accessible areas to children and near food in the classrooms. This was corrected when cleaning supplies were removed near food and inaccessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Installation of Unitary Surfacing Materials - to Manufacturer's Specifications: The outside playground has unitary surfacing that has not been properly maintained and contained holes and rips in the surfacing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation of Unitary Surfacing Materials - to Manufacturer's Specifications (26 TAC §746.4911(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A schooler was observed to be unsupervised when going to the restroom in another room while the caregiver remained in the playscape area.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: A caregiver was observed on their personal cell phone when caring for children during naptime. This was corrected when the cell  phone was put up.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points: The toddler play area in the playscape has a broken piece of play equipment that has sharp edges.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - No Pinch, Crush, or Shear Points (26 TAC §746.4601(7))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: In the 18 to 23 months old class, documentation showing each child's age was not readily available in the classroom for caregivers to retrieve. Caregiver was unable to cofirm children's ages.  This was corrected when the assistant director had to retrieve an attendance sheet with the birthdays to find the children's ages.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: In the Toddler class for 18 to 23 months old, documentation showing each child's age was not readily available in the classroom for caregivers to retrieve. This was corrected when the assistant director had to retrieve an attendance sheet with the birthdays to find the children's ages.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: Based on investigation findings, corporal punishment was practiced towards children in care with the use a pointer instructional tool.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Based on investigation findings, a caregiver is yelling at children when addressing challenging behavior.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Harsh, Abusive or Profane Language: Based on the investigation findings, profane language is used around children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: Based on investigation findings, inappropriate grabbing as a prohibited punishment is practiced at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records: During the morning period, two caregivers were present and did not have any access to child or personnel records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records (26 TAC §746.1013(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: In the 18m to 2yr classroom, there were 16 children total with 1 caregiver that transitioned from the gym to the classroom. The special age group number was 2 years old. This was corrected when the director had transitioned and stayed in the classroom until another caregiver arrived.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: It was found that there has not been a recent fire inspection conducted nor any fire inspection scheduled with the fire marshal. The last inspection was on 2/3/25 expiring by 2/3/26.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: During the morning time while breakfast was being served and eaten, screen time was being utilized from children 2 too 4 years old.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements: One caregiver did not have education documentation in their file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records- Meets Requirements (26 TAC §746.901(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Medical Authorization: Three children's files were reviewed and found that there was no emergency medical authorization/consent signed by parent/guardian.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Physician Information (26 TAC §746.605(11))

occurrences.finding: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children: During the morning time, the total amount of children in the gym was 34 kids from 18 months old to 12 years old with two caregivers. The specific age group was 3 years old. The children were in the gym from 6:30AM to 8:00AM which exceeds the 45 minutes for opening and breakfast time is from 6:30AM to 7:30AM.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1609)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: Four children's records were reviewed and found that there were no health statements for the children who had been enrolled past 12 months.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Health Statement (26 TAC §746.603(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Admission Information: Three children's files were missing additional admission information.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Admission Information (26 TAC §746.603(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2912): One caregiver who was hired 1/2025, did not have a pre-employment affidavit.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2912) (26 TAC §746.901(5))

occurrences.finding: Provide Parents With Copy of Policies: One child's file did not have policy acknowledgement.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Provide Parents With Copy of Policies (26 TAC §746.503)

occurrences.finding: Required Records Storage: Two children's records were not kept for 3 months after the two children disenrolled on 7/2025 and 8/2025.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Storage (26 TAC §746.803(a))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: Based on the information obtained for the investigation, there is sufficient evidence to suggest that proper parental notification of minor injuries was not maintained.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: Based on the findings of a recent DFPS investigation, there was evidence to suggest that corporal punishment is being used in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: The center did not report the number of employees that left employment in 2024 by the required date of 1/15/25
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: A caregiver was observed supervising children in a class without a current cpr/first aid license.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records: 3 of the 4 caregivers folders were observed to be incomplete. Cpr/first aid license, discipline and guidance form and current trainings.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §746.901)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Based on the information received, there is sufficient information to suggest that a caregiver had been yelling and calling children names as a form of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Operational Policies - Inform Parents That They May Visit Center Anytime During Operating Hours: The operation policy states the parents should arrange a time to visit and conferences would need an appointment. It also states that parents would be interrupting the classroom during the class day.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Operational Policies - Inform Parents That They May Visit Center Anytime During Operating Hours (26 TAC §746.501(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Minimum Standards: 2 of the 6 classrooms observed during walk through caregivers did not know how many children were in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Minimum Standards (26 TAC §746.1203(1))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits: Children were observed sleeping at the door when entering the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits (26 TAC §746.2909(1))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Fire Inspection: The fire inspection was not available for review during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Fire Inspection (26 TAC §746.5103)

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022 revealed  that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022 as required.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))

occurrences.finding: Operational Policies - Inform Parents That They May Visit Center Anytime During Operating Hours: This standard was investigated in regards to a report received and compliance was not met.    The center does not have an open door policy that allows parents to visit the center at any time during the hours of operation to observe their child, center's program activities, building, premises, and the equipment without having to secure prior approval.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Operational Policies - Inform Parents That They May Visit Center Anytime During Operating Hours (26 TAC §746.501(b)(1))
